svg.font-family: Inter, Liberation Sans, Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif
svg.title: karyon: every representation
svg.desc: A karyon sheet of 22 panels in 3 columns: panel A, Ideogram, coverage, reference, genes, variants, ruler; panel B, Read pileup with mismatches against the reference; panel C, Sequence logos: information content and enrichment/depletion; panel D, Association statistics and a genotype matrix; panel E, Dotplot and synteny ribbons between two sequences; panel F, Multiple sequence alignment, coloured by residue class; panel G, Variable sites with the phylogeny that orders them; panel H, A tree on its own; panel I, Windowed statistics read against a baseline they can fall below; panel J, A circular chromosome: annotation, composition, and chords across the middle; panel K, Raw nanopore current, with the bases a basecaller made of it; panel L, One locus in three genomes: the deletion that made BCG a vaccine; panel M, Methylation per site, one lane per strand, faded by read depth; panel N, A whole draft assembly on one axis, every contig of it; panel O, Structural variants as arcs between their breakpoints; panel P, Six reading frames: the stops, and what is open between them; panel Q, Two trees face to face, and where they disagree; panel R, Methylation one molecule at a time, not one fraction per site; panel S, A coding sequence read as protein, and the variants named by residue; panel T, One molecule, three alignments, and the order it visited them in; panel U, Genomic intervals painted onto the branch that gained or lost them; panel V, Transcription units: one arrow, one molecule, one hairpin.
